## Summary

I extended the business-day rule for the registration date to skip listed public holidays, placing the change where it belongs — in the `BusinessDay` calendar helper, which is the single authority for what counts as a business day.

**`util/BusinessDay.java`** — added the fixed public-holiday set and folded it into `isBusinessDay`:
- New `PUBLIC_HOLIDAYS` set: `2026-01-01, 2026-01-26, 2026-04-25, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-28`.
- New `isPublicHoliday(date)` predicate.

- `onOrAfter` needed no logic change: its existing roll-forward loop now automatically skips holidays too (e.g. Fri 2026-12-25 → weekend → Mon 2026-12-28, also a holiday → Tue 2026-12-29).

Because every downstream step (`ResolveRegistrationDate`, daily-limit, bulk-signup, membership number, tenure) already keys off the adjusted date via `onOrAfter`, no other production code needed touching. I updated the `ResolveRegistrationDate` javadoc to reflect the extended rule.

**`test/util/BusinessDayTest.java`** (new) — 9 unit tests covering weekdays, weekends, each holiday's roll-forward, and the chained Christmas/28th case. The existing black-box `AcceptanceTest` continues to pass.

No single class became a catch-all — the holiday calendar lives with the rest of the calendar rules, and each step keeps its single responsibility.
